types.purpose: A message the reader must see before going on, set in an alert: what changed, what it costs, what to do.
A Badge: a short status word pinned to a thing, never a sentence.

do: Give it the two colours as token names or as literals — hex, `rgb()`, `oklch()`, `white`, `black` — and it reports the contrast ratio with its grade.

types.purpose: One action, stated as a verb. A link when href is set, a button otherwise.

dont: A button has no form, so its `onSuccess.type` can only be `navigate`, and its `onError` only a `toast`; anything else is refused when the configuration is read.

It applies to a `button` placed on a record of a table — in a list's row template, or in a single-record container or a page bound to one record — and is refused at startup outside any record binding; the same pair is accepted by a button field and by a table's row actions.

The record must be a row of a declared table: a `disabledWhen` on a button or row action whose rows come from a `system` source or a `collection` page, one in the page `layout`, and one inside a template placed from `app.components` would never be judged, so each is refused at startup too.

`disabledReason`, which accepts `$record.<field>` and a `$t:` key, shows in a tooltip on hover and on focus and is announced as the button's description; without it the button is disabled with no explanation, and a `disabledReason` without `disabledWhen` is refused.
An automation a disabled control would start is refused with 409 `ACTION_DISABLED` and the reason when the press names its record; a hidden one answers 404, as an absent one does.
It is refused at startup anywhere else.
What a control cannot do is refused rather than ignored.

A button, a table row action or a menu item has no form, so its `onSuccess.type` can only be `navigate`, and the keys that describe a form — `preserveFields`, `title`, `message`, `actions`, `showSummary`, `redirect` — are refused there.

An `onSuccess.navigate` naming another site (`https://…`) is refused on every control — a button, a row action, a menu item, an endpoint form, a file upload and a form alike — because an answered action moves the reader within the app; a link sends them elsewhere.

types.purpose: A Button Group: several exclusive actions of equal weight, joined so they read as one control.
Navigation inside a run of text, underlined so it reads as a link at a glance.

dont: The two keys are useless apart and are refused apart at startup, as is a comparison between two literals — it answers the same on every render, so either every item of the set is current or none is.

types.purpose: The one control that flips the colour scheme and remembers the choice.
A calendar: a month of days to pick one date, a range, or several, inline on the page.

dont: It was named `calendar`; a config still writing `type: calendar` is refused with a message naming `event-calendar`, and renaming the `type` is the whole migration.
An event takes one colour, from one option, so `colorField` must name a `single-select`: a `multi-select` is refused when the config is read, naming the field.

types.purpose: A yes or no the reader sets in a checkbox, with room for several in a list.

guidance.usage: Use `switch` when the change takes effect immediately, and `checkbox` when it takes effect on submit — the two look similar and read very differently to someone deciding whether to press Save.

types.purpose: Source text the reader edits, highlighted by language and indented to your width.

dont: `maxLines` must not be below it: the two bound the same box from opposite sides, so an inverted pair is refused at boot.

types.purpose: One choice found by typing into a combobox, from a list that narrows with each keystroke.

dont: `chips` requires `multiple: true` and is refused without it, and on a `select`.
`searchable` and `native` are refused (the browser's own control is `native-select`).

types.purpose: A Date Picker: a calendar date, typed or picked, in the reader's locale.
A period rather than a date: two months side by side, and presets that resolve against today.

do: Reach for `date-picker` with `datePickerMode: range` when you want a range in one calendar and no presets; reach for this when the period is the point — a reporting window, a stay, a billing month.
dont: `value` takes that same notation, and a **preset name is refused there by pattern**.

types.purpose: A labelled control with its help and its error, laid out the same way in every field.
A single line of text, typed by the reader into an input.

dont: A one-time code is its own type, [`input-otp`](#input-otp); `inputType: one-time-code` is refused with a message naming it.

types.purpose: One input with a fixed prefix, suffix or action fused to its edge, in one input group.
A short verification code typed into an input OTP, one character per box, pasted or autofilled.

dont: `inputType` is refused: an `input-otp` is always a one-time code.

types.purpose: The label of one form control, wired to it so a click on the name focuses the control.
One choice in a native select, the browser's own dropdown, with no script to load.

do: Keep `select` on a marketing page or a public form, where the control carries your design.
dont: `searchable`, `searchPlaceholder` and `allowCustomValue` are refused (type-ahead is [`combobox`](#combobox)), and so is an option `icon`, which an `<option>` element cannot paint.

types.purpose: One choice among a few in a radio group, all visible at once.

guidance.usage: Use `switch` when the change takes effect immediately, and `checkbox` when it takes effect on submit — the two look similar and read very differently to someone deciding whether to press Save.

types.purpose: A row of stars that reads a rating, and writes a whole one inside a form.
One row of another table, found by typing its name and linked.

do: Reach for `record-picker` when the page has no such column to dispatch from — a filter bar, a panel, a step that writes somewhere else.

types.reason: Searches a table of yours and links the row it finds. This page is bound to no table — and binding it to one of yours is what the confidentiality bound forbids — so there are no candidates for it to offer. Its states, its paging and its create path are drawn as authored option sections on its own page.

types.purpose: Formatted prose, written in place, with only the marks you allow.

dont: The toolbar vocabulary is closed — `bold`, `italic`, `strike`, `heading`, `list`, `ordered-list`, `code-block`, `blockquote`, `link`, `image`, `table`, `horizontal-rule` — so a typo is refused when the config is decoded rather than dropped silently at mount.

types.purpose: One choice among many in a select, folded until opened.

dont: `searchable`, `searchPlaceholder` and `allowCustomValue` are refused on a `select`, each with a message naming `combobox`, and `native` with one naming `native-select`.
`options` and `dataSource` are **mutually exclusive** — both answer "what are the choices", so declaring the two together is refused at startup.
The table-backed and endpoint-backed forms are alternatives, not a pair: a binding declaring both `table` and `system` is refused at startup.
Both keys are required, and the field must be one of the three choice types; a table or field the app does not declare, or a field of another type, is refused at startup.

types.purpose: A well to sign in, or a typed name, stored once with the statement agreed to.
types.reason: A well to sign in, or a name to type, under the statement being agreed to. Pressing Sign uploads the mark and writes it onto the record the page is bound to, so the pad is a write path of its own, and a read-only console may carry none. Once signed it reads "Signed by … on …" from that record. See it on a data-bound page.

types.purpose: A number in a range, dragged along a slider rather than typed.
A setting that applies as soon as its switch flips.

guidance.usage: Use `switch` when the change takes effect immediately, and `checkbox` when it takes effect on submit — the two look similar and read very differently to someone deciding whether to press Save.

types.purpose: Several lines of text in a textarea, growing with what is written.
A pressed or released toggle that holds its state.
A toggle group: a row of toggles where one, or several, stay pressed.
A Carousel: slides on one track, moved through one at a time with arrows, dots or a swipe.

dont: `layout` is refused (a `carousel` is always one track), and `gridColumns` and `featured` are refused because they belong to a grid, which stays a `gallery`.
A `gallery` with `layout: carousel` is refused with a message naming `carousel`.

types.purpose: A Chart over rows: bars, lines, areas or a donut, one series per colour.

dont: A second `series` entry has nothing to draw and is refused at boot, naming `series` and `chartAggregate`.

types.purpose: Records on a month or week grid, placed by their date field.
One set of conditions, published to every data component bound to the same channel.
The fields you declare, written to the table it binds or posted to an endpoint you name.

do: Use a top-level `forms[]` entry when the form **takes something in**: a submission that deserves its own address, a record in the Submissions inbox, protection against spam, an opening window or a cap, its own access rule, a one-question or multi-step layout, or an automation that starts when it is submitted.
Use the page `form` component when the form **works on data already inside the app**: editing the record the page shows, posting to an endpoint of your own, or signing someone in or up.
dont: A name the form does not draw, or one listed in two sections, is refused when the config loads.

types.reason: Renders a live submit control — over the fields you declare on it, or writing a record back to the table it binds; a preview frame may carry no write path (ADR-022 A3 clause 2).

types.purpose: Records as cards with an image, in a responsive grid.

dont: One walkable track is its own type, [`carousel`](#carousel); `layout: carousel` is refused with a message naming it.
Any other action is refused when the config is decoded.
`layout` is refused (a `carousel` is always one track), and `gridColumns` and `featured` are refused because they belong to a grid, which stays a `gallery`.
A `gallery` with `layout: carousel` is refused with a message naming `carousel`.

types.purpose: Nodes in ordered columns with the edges between them: the things the system read `dataSource` names, laid out left to right by kind, so an operator can follow a path rather than look a pair up.

guidance.usage: Reach for it when the question is _how_ something is reached rather than _whether_ it is — a path a reader can follow with a finger, through whatever stands in the middle.
do: Reach for a `matrix` when the answer is a lookup, and for a `chart` when the answer is a quantity: no `chartType` draws nodes and edges, because every one of them plots a value against an axis.

types.purpose: Records as cards in columns, one column per value of a select field.

dont: Any other action is refused when the config is decoded — put richer behaviour on the drawer's footer actions instead.
The lane field is checked against the bound table, so a typo is refused by `sovrium validate` rather than drawing one lane per record.

types.purpose: One number that matters, with its label and its movement.
Records as rows with a title, a subtitle and a trailing value.
Records placed as pins at their location, with a list twin a keyboard can use.
Two sets of things crossed, each intersection a glyph rather than a word: rows and columns are nodes of the graph `dataSource` names, and a cell is the edge between them.

guidance.usage: Reach for it when the question is _which of these reach which of those, and how strongly_ — permissions across roles, features across plans, coverage across teams.
do: Reach for a `table` instead when the cells are values a reader needs to read word by word.

types.purpose: A questionnaire: one question per screen, answered by choosing, with a count of how many remain.
types.reason: Submits each answer through the form it names; a preview frame may carry no write path (ADR-022 A3 clause 2).

types.purpose: A Data Table: the records of a table as a grid — sorting, filtering, grouping, selection, paging — or the rows you write in the config.

do: Use a `sheet` with `dataSource.system` and its own `recordFields`, opened with `onRowClick: { action: openSheet, component }`.
Use it for a summary grid — the latest orders on a dashboard — whose rows are edited elsewhere.
dont: Bind it to a table or to a read endpoint with `dataSource`, or omit the binding and it draws the `tableHeaders` and `tableRows` you author; declaring both is refused.
A `toolbar` or a `search` key on a `table` is refused at load, naming that replacement, and a refresh button becomes `dataSource.refreshMode`.

**`rowExpand` and `onRowClick` cannot both be declared.** A row has one click, and two answers to what it does is a config whose halves cannot both apply — so it is refused rather than one silently winning.
A rule with neither is refused.
`tableColumns` belongs to written tables only: declared beside a `dataSource` it is refused, as `tableRows` is.

When a bulk action or a row action is refused because the reader's writes were too many, the grid shows a toast saying so and in how many seconds to retry, in the page's language, whatever `onError` declares; the rows, the selection and the buttons stay as they were.
A grid must start with at least one field column drawn, or the config is refused when it loads.

Naming the same field at two levels is refused at validation: every record in a group already shares the value that group was formed on, so a repeated level puts exactly one sub-group inside each group and partitions nothing.

The view owns the filter, the sort, the grouping and the visible fields, so a view-bound grid may not repeat them: a `dataSource.filter`, `dataSource.sort` or `dataSource.fields` beside `view` is refused when the config loads, with a message naming the view.

No page size may exceed 100, the rows per page the records API serves: a larger `pageSize` or `pageSizeOptions` entry is refused at validation, naming the number and the ceiling, rather than failing the first time a reader picks it.

types.purpose: The records of one table nested under their parents, opened branch by branch.

dont: A batch update is judged as if all its moves had landed, so two moves that close a loop only together are refused, and the whole batch with them.

types.purpose: An aspect ratio frame: one image, video or map held at a fixed width-to-height shape, whatever the screen.
A Card: a bounded surface for one thing, on the page background.

guidance.usage: Use it when one page has to show two design systems at once.
dont: `variant: bubble` and `side` are refused on a `card`, each with a message naming `bubble`.

types.purpose: A box that gives its children padding and a width.
Children in a row or a column, spaced by one gap.
Children in equal columns, collapsing to one on a narrow screen.
A message scroller: the scroll frame of a conversation, opening at the latest turn and keeping its place.
Resizable panels: two side by side, with a draggable handle between them.

dont: It was named `split-pane`; a config still writing `type: split-pane` is refused with a message naming `resizable`, and renaming the `type` is the whole migration.

types.purpose: The Sidebar: the left rail of grouped navigation, with an active entry.
An attachment chip: one file drawn by its icon or thumbnail, its name and size, and a way to open it.
An audio file with play, progress and duration.

dont: A `target` naming no `video` or `audio` on its page is refused at startup, unless it is built from the record (`clip-$record.id`).

types.purpose: A Code Block: source text in a monospace frame, highlighted by language, with a copy button.
A stored file shown inline: a PDF in its viewer, an image with zoom, else a download.
types.reason: Shows a stored file inline: an image with zoom, a PDF in its viewer, anything else as a download. Every face is drawn from a file signed for the reader, and the only files this instance holds are in your buckets, which this console may not read. See it on a data-bound page.

types.purpose: One glyph from the app's icon set, sized and coloured by the text around it.
Another page embedded at a fixed height.
types.reason: Not drawn here, and this is a refusal rather than a gap: this console renders every specimen flat, in one document, because a design system inside a nested scrolling document is not one a reader can read. Drawing an iframe specimen would put the frame back. Look at the page you embedded it on.

types.purpose: A picture with its alt text, lazy unless it is above the fold.

do: Give every image `width` and `height`: the browser then reserves its box before the file arrives and nothing below it moves — layout shift is the second of those metrics.
Give every image that carries meaning a real `alt`.

types.purpose: The keys a reader is meant to press, drawn as Kbd keycaps.
A value drawn as a scannable code.

do: Give every symbol an `aria-label`.

types.purpose: Search within the page, or filter a bound list as you type.

dont: A box declaring neither, or both, is refused at load.
`scope: subscribers`, where a sibling named this box's id, was removed in 0.39 and is refused at load, naming `publishes`.

types.purpose: Typography: a run of prose at one step of the type scale.
The headings of the page as a list that follows the reader.
A video file with a poster, play and progress.
An Accordion: stacked sections that open one at a time.
An Avatar: a person or a thing as a small round mark — a picture, initials, or nothing at all.

dont: `size` is `default` (32px) by default, with `sm` at 24px and `lg` at 40px — `md` is refused with a message naming `default`; `shape` is `circle` for people and `square` for a record or an organisation.

types.purpose: A Bubble: the surface of one chat turn, set to its side of the thread.
A collapsible region behind one trigger, shown or hidden in place, with no siblings to close.
Pairs of a term and its detail, read down rather than across.
An Empty state: what a view says when it has nothing to show, and what to do about it.

dont: It was named `empty-state`; a config still writing `type: empty-state` is refused with a message naming `empty`, and renaming the `type` is the whole migration.

types.purpose: An Item: one row of a list — a leading mark, a title, a subtitle, a trailing value.

dont: It was named `list-item`; a config still writing `type: list-item` is refused with a message naming `item`, and renaming the `type` is the whole migration.

types.purpose: A marker line inside a thread or a list: a status, a system note, a labelled break.
A strip of logos or words that scrolls sideways.

do: Use it to show more items than fit on screen — a row of screenshots, a set of logos — as a demonstration rather than a static grid.

types.purpose: A message: one turn of a conversation — who said it, when, on which side — around the bubble that holds it.
One field of one record, drawn read-only in its own format.

guidance.usage: Reach for it inside a record-bound region when the value should carry its field type's formatting — a currency as currency, a relation as a link, a status as its coloured chip.

types.reason: Draws ONE field of the record the page it sits on is bound to. This page is bound to no record — and binding it to one of yours is what the confidentiality bound forbids — so there is nothing for it to read. The field CONTROLS it draws from are in the composed form below.

types.purpose: A Scroll Area: a region that scrolls inside the page with a thin scrollbar.
One task split into ordered steps, each a body of its own, with a rail that shows progress.
One colour drawn as a filled square with its value and its name.

do: Give it the token by **name** — a custom property under the name your stylesheet reads it by, such as `--primary`, `--background`, `--muted-foreground`, `--chart-1` or `--sidebar-primary`, or a step from a design ramp such as `neutral-500`.
Use it for a role token, which is redeclared per scheme.

types.purpose: Tabs: a short list of views, one visible at a time.

dont: **`panels` and `children` must be the same length** when both are present; a different number of each is refused at startup by name.

types.purpose: Events on a line: declared in the config, or every record of a table between two dates.

dont: The change is one ordinary record update, so the table's field rules, automations and webhooks apply; the bar moves at once and goes back if the update is refused.
**`children` and `dataSource` are mutually exclusive.** A timeline declaring both is refused at validation.

types.purpose: A Breadcrumb: where the reader is, as a path they can climb back up.

dont: Declaring `breadcrumbItems` and `derive` together is refused at startup — there is no defensible precedence between an authored trail and a derived one.
`home` on an enumerated trail is refused at startup, because such a trail already states its own first item.
Like `labels`, `unlinked` requires `derive` and is refused at startup without it — on an enumerated trail, leave `href` off the item instead.

types.purpose: A Command palette: search everything from anywhere, opened with a keyboard shortcut.

dont: It was named `command-palette`; a config still writing `type: command-palette` is refused with a message naming `command`, and renaming the `type` is the whole migration.

types.purpose: A Context Menu of actions on the thing under the pointer, opened on right click.
A Dropdown Menu of actions gathered behind one button, opened on click.

do: Give it `toggle: checked` or `toggle: unchecked` and it renders as a two-state row — label on the left, switch on the right — that a reader can flip without the menu closing.

types.purpose: A Menubar: a row of menus, as in a desktop application.
A Navigation Menu: the top navigation of a site, with menus that open on hover.
Pagination: move between the pages of a long list.
An Alert Dialog asking the reader to confirm an action that loses data.

do: Use it for what cannot be undone — deleting an account or everything in a workspace — and make it something the reader knows, such as `$session.email` or `$record.name`, rather than a fixed word.

types.purpose: A Dialog holding a focused task over the page, dismissed by the overlay or a button.

dont: `component` must name a `dialog` declared on the same page; an id no dialog carries is refused when the config loads.
**Migrating from `modal`.** The `modal` component type has been removed, and a config still naming it is refused at startup with a message pointing here.

types.purpose: A drawer: a panel that rises from the bottom edge and is dragged down to dismiss.
A Hover Card: a preview that opens when the pointer rests on a name.
A Popover: a small panel anchored to its trigger, opened on click.
A Sheet: a panel that slides in from an edge and keeps the page visible behind it.

do: Give a sheet a `dataSource` and it becomes record-bound: it fetches one record, renders a control per field, and — unless you turn editing off — saves back through the record API.
dont: A sheet bound to a system detail endpoint whose read is refused or fails says the same, without Retry: a refused read is not asked again.
`operation: create` is refused when the config is read, because a footer has no form to fill and acts on a record that already exists; put a form in a dialog instead.
A `visibleWhen.field` the sheet's table does not have is refused when the config is read.
These shapes are refused when the app boots, each because the failure would otherwise be silent:

types.purpose: A Toast, drawn by Sonner: a short confirmation that leaves on its own.
A Tooltip: one line of help on hover or focus.
A Progress bar: how far a known task has run.
A Skeleton: the shape of content that is still loading.
A Spinner: waiting, when nothing else can be shown.

do: Reach for `skeleton` rather than `spinner` when you know the shape of what is loading: a placeholder that matches the eventual layout does not make the page jump when the content lands.

types.purpose: A Separator: a hairline between two things that are not the same thing.

dont: It was named `divider`; a config still writing `type: divider` is refused with a message naming `separator`, and renaming the `type` is the whole migration.

types.purpose: Empty room, sized from the spacing ladder.
The thread of comments on a record, with replies, sorting and a composer.

dont: A parent that does not exist, or that belongs to another record — top-level or not — is refused with the same `404`, and nothing is stored; a parent on the same record that is itself a reply is refused with `422`.
A config still saying `type: commentCount` is refused at startup with that instruction.

types.reason: Hydrates a comment composer — a form with a live submit control that posts a comment onto a record. A read-only console may carry no write path, so it is named here rather than drawn. It renders on your own pages.

types.purpose: One field type drawn in every state the console documents it in.
types.reason: Has no appearance of its own: it draws whatever control the fieldType you name gets, so a card here would document one field type instead of this component. The field types are all drawn, in every state, in the field catalogue.

types.purpose: Files into a bucket, dropped or picked.

dont: A compact upload takes no drop zone, and `compact: true` together with `dropZone: true` is refused when the config loads.

types.purpose: Change the language of the page.
types.reason: Draws the languages an app declares in languages[]. This console’s own surface app declares none — it carries your design system and deliberately nothing else — so the component has no list to draw. It renders on your pages.

types.purpose: A number, typed or stepped one unit at a time.

do: Prefer `number-input` over an `input` with `inputType: number` when the value is genuinely counted — it gives keyboard and pointer affordances a text box does not.

types.purpose: One option of one type, drawn at the value you name, so a setting can be seen rather than described.

dont: An option path the type does not publish is refused, naming the paths it does publish.

types.purpose: Rows the reader can drag into a new order.
One component drawn as an exhibit, framed and labelled for the catalogue.

dont: Both are refused when the config is read, so the failure names the reason instead of silently drawing nothing.

types.reason: A frame around a drawn component and the config that produced it. It refuses to hold another one — each level would print the level below, with no bottom — so it cannot be drawn inside this page. Every card here is one.

types.purpose: A time of day, typed or picked.
A thread with an agent declared in agents[].
